name: Treaty with the Menominee, 1836 (Treaty of the Cedars)
promises: Article 1: the Menominee ceded the country between the Wolf River, the Menominee River and Green Bay, and a strip on the upper Wisconsin River, as bounded in the treaty.

Article 2: $20,000 a year for twenty years, and each year of that term $3,000 of provisions, 2,000 pounds of tobacco, thirty barrels of salt, $500 for farming tools and stock, and two blacksmiths with shops.
Article 2: the tribe's debts on an annexed schedule, $99,710.50, to be paid after the Commissioner of Indian Affairs examined each, any surplus to go to the tribe.
today: No Indian Claims Commission decision for the Menominee was found in Oklahoma State University's collection, and none of the Menominee Court of Claims opinions of 1941 to 1952 (95, 97, 101, 102, 107, 117, 118, 119 and 121 Ct. Cl.) that were opened concerns this treaty; they deal with swamp lands, timber and trust fund interest under later acts.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe publishes the full text of the 1836 treaty among its historical documents, alongside its treaties of 1848, 1854 and 1856 and the Termination and Restoration Acts.

openQuestions: Audit 2026-11-08: the payment articles were read from the OSU text and set out in the promises; dates and 7 Stat. 506 checked. No Court of Claims opinion in the Caselaw Access Project (95 to 121 Ct. Cl.) mentions this treaty.
The Menominee had a special jurisdictional act (September 3, 1935) instead of an Indian Claims Commission docket; whether any claim under it concerned the 1836 price was not found.
No Menominee narrative of this treaty was found on the Tribe's site; its College or Historic Preservation office may have one.

plain.promised: The United States would pay $20,000 a year for twenty years plus goods and blacksmiths, and pay the tribe's debts, for a large Menominee cession around Green Bay and the Wolf and Menominee rivers.
plain.happened: No court, claims commission or government finding about this treaty was found.
plain.today: The Menominee publish the treaty text; no claim about its price was found.
